premises.text: Open and free software commonly has bugs and missing features, and support is hard to get
premises.evidence_span: all this software has two properties in common, which is bugs and missing features. And especially when it's open or free software, support can be hard to get

premises.text: There is a mismatch in knowledge and priority between users and developers
premises.evidence_span: what we have is a mismatch in knowledge and priority between the user and the developer

premises.text: Integrations put a panel on major issue systems so users can place an incentive in two clicks
premises.evidence_span: we offer integrations for all the major issue systems. So it's an integration, shows a panel, as you can see on the right-hand side. So with two clicks, a user can place an incentive

premises.text: Multiple users can crowdfund one issue, and developers can ask for an incentive or list it for crowdfunding
premises.evidence_span: many users can place incentives on one issue. So crowdfunding is now a reality

premises.text: The platform takes a 6% fee on successful incentives and shares fees with issue-system hosters
premises.evidence_span: we take a 6% fee for each successful incentive. And we offer a fee to all the issue system hosters running our integration

value.text: Users get on-demand software support by placing incentives on issues
value.evidence_span: makes it possible to place incentives for on demand software support

secondary_value.text: Adding a monetization element to the open source market
secondary_value.evidence_span: we are adding a monetization element to the entire open source market

secondary_value.text: Issue systems become a profit center for hosters
secondary_value.evidence_span: turns an issue system into a profit center

causal_links.evidence_span: To overcome this, we are offering a service which allows you to pay or get paid directly from an issue page
how do I get support for this software
pay or get paid directly from an issue page

notes: Need/product/fee triad retained because support mismatch, issue integrations, and hoster fee-share are separately revisable. Developer-side one-click ask folded into crowdfunding premise (v1.3.2 §4.1(5)). App-store next focus treated as roadmap vision, not a premise. Market-size figures excluded as framing.
